text:
[What] When the same sound is repeated at high frequency, the ear hears the repetition rate as a pitch. This tool turns one key into a vertical chain (same x, spread along the time axis); while playing, the chain triggers at the given rate so you hear that pitch - give each key a different pitch and the chart plays a melody.

[Options]
- BPM: keep it the same as the chart; used to convert beats to seconds.
- Fill note type: tap/drag/flick/hold/same as input (default) - the type of the generated notes.
- Preview: synthesizes the whole passage with a sawtooth wave and plays it; a playback progress line is drawn on the canvas.
- Refresh view: redraws the canvas from the current input JSON.

[Count rules]
- Unit note length = 1 / pitch frequency (to hear that pitch you must repeat at that interval); pitch 0 (single key) falls back to a 16th note (60/bpm/4).
- Hold: count = duration x frequency, derived from BPM and pitch, not editable by hand; the pieces connect head-to-tail.
- Glide (pitch A->B): the repetition rate changes linearly, total = duration x (fA+fB)/2 and each time is solved from the integral of f, so the chain gets denser or sparser.
- Other notes: the count is manual; the first note stays in place and the rest follow one unit apart.

[Usage] Left-click a note to set pitch; right-click a hold for its end pitch, others for count; 0 = single key. The editor is embedded in the canvas with the caret placed there; Enter or clicking elsewhere saves, Esc cancels.
- Canvas: earlier time at the bottom, later on top; horizontal axis is the x coordinate (+/-675, note width 175), the time grid is in beats with one spare beat above and below; mouse wheel scrolls time, Ctrl+wheel zooms time.

[Audio] The preview uses a sawtooth wave (richest harmonics, easiest to hear the pitch); glides are rendered with a linear pitch change.
